title: DECam Deep View of the Antlia Cluster
caption: The Antlia Cluster of galaxies, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
celestial: Antlia Cluster · constellation Antlia · about 130 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Image processing: R. Colombari & M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two big elliptical galaxies dominate this deep view of the Antlia Cluster: NGC 3268 at the centre and NGC 3258 at lower right. Around them lies a crowd of other galaxies, for the cluster, also catalogued as Abell S636, holds at least 230 members about 130 million light-years away toward the constellation Antlia, the Air Pump.

The cluster contains a rich mix of galaxy types: lenticular galaxies, irregular galaxies and ultra-compact dwarfs are all present. A galaxy cluster is a large gathering of galaxies bound together by gravity, and it can bring together galaxies of very different shapes.

The picture was taken with the 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera (DECam) on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, located at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile. It captures only part of the cluster, yet its ultra-deep view shows galaxies both within Antlia and far beyond it in fine detail.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (48.44 x 34.91 arcminutes) and distance (130 million light years), the frame spans roughly 1.8 million × 1.3 million light-years. Its light set out about 130 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken in optical light through g, r and i filters with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope; the colour mapping isn't published.
